cultural.summary: Grow a tough, ICAR-tested variety that naturally shrugs off the yellow vein virus!
cultural.how: Plant Parbhani Kranti or Ghana selection both found highly resistant in ICAR field screening of 14 okra cultivars.

cultural.summary: Sow a little earlier to dodge the peak whitefly rush before it even begins!
cultural.how: Adjust sowing to an earlier date within the recommended window, since early sowing has shown reduced YVMV incidence in field trials.

cultural.summary: Clear out sneaky weeds around your field where whiteflies love to hide!
cultural.how: Remove weed hosts from in and around the field.

cultural.summary: The moment a plant shows yellow veins, give it a swift, caring send-off to protect the rest!
cultural.how: Uproot and destroy infected plants immediately, away from the garden (not in compost).

biological.summary: Hang cheerful yellow traps to catch and count sneaky whiteflies before they spread trouble!
biological.how: Hang yellow sticky traps around the field/canopy to trap and monitor whitefly.

botanical.summary: A gentle neem mist keeps whitefly numbers down and virus spread slower!
botanical.how: Apply a neem-based product spray around sowing time and repeat regularly.

local_practice.summary: A traditional cow urine spray farmers trust to keep plants strong and pests away!
local_practice.how: Spray 10% cow urine solution on the plant.

iks.summary: A powerful fermented neem-and-cow-gift potion, brewed the traditional way!
iks.how: Ferment 5kg crushed neem leaves + 100L water + 5L cow urine + 2kg fresh cow dung, stirring twice daily for 48 hours in shade, then strain. Makes enough for 1 acre.

cultural.summary: Give your soil a break from okra every couple of years to starve out leftover fungus!
cultural.how: Avoid continuous okra cropping in the same field.

cultural.summary: Sweep away sick fallen leaves so spores don't get a second chance!
cultural.how: Remove and destroy infected leaf debris.

cultural.summary: Give each plant room to breathe so fresh air keeps fungus away!
cultural.how: Ensure adequate plant spacing at sowing time.

biological.summary: The single most powerful microbe mist tested spray it on to keep leaf spots away!
biological.how: Spray Pseudomonas fluorescens at 5% concentration on foliage.

biological.summary: A gentle beneficial-fungus spray that keeps leaf spots from spreading!
biological.how: Spray Trichoderma viride at 5% concentration on foliage.

biological.summary: Two friendly microbes teaming up for the strongest leaf spot defense!
biological.how: Combine Trichoderma (2%) + Pseudomonas fluorescens (2%) and spray together.

botanical.summary: A classic neem oil spray to keep leaf spots from taking hold!
botanical.how: Spray neem oil at 5% concentration on foliage.

botanical.summary: A zesty garlic oil mist that fungi really don't enjoy!
botanical.how: Spray garlic oil at 4% concentration on foliage.

botanical.summary: A sharp onion oil spray adding extra leaf spot protection!
botanical.how: Spray onion oil at 4% concentration on foliage.

local_practice.summary: The winning traditional combo! Seeds get a special bath, then leaves get a gentle five-gift spray!
local_practice.how: Treat seeds with Beejamrit at 200ml/kg seed before sowing, then follow with 3 foliar sprays of Panchagavya at 10% concentration.
local_practice.frequency: Seed treatment once; foliar spray 3 times at 15-day intervals from disease onset

cultural.summary: Choose well-drained ground so little roots never sit in soggy soil!
Check the soil before watering so seedlings get just what they need, not too much!
cultural.how: Avoid overwatering nursery beds; check soil moisture before each watering.

cultural.summary: A fluffy vermicompost or farmyard-manure mix gives seedlings a healthy home!
cultural.how: Use vermicompost + soil or FYM + soil as potting media.

biological.summary: A soil treatment of friendly bacteria to keep tiny roots safe from rot!
biological.how: Apply Pseudomonas fluorescens to the soil at sowing.

biological.summary: Coat seeds in a helpful fungus before planting to block disease from day one!
biological.how: Treat seed with Trichoderma harzianum before sowing.

botanical.summary: Surprise! Garlic extract beat neem in real trials for protecting roots from rot!
botanical.how: Apply garlic clove extract at sowing/early seedling stage.

botanical.summary: A trusty neem extract, second only to garlic in keeping seedlings safe!
botanical.how: Apply neem leaf/seed extract at sowing/early seedling stage.

local_practice.note: No documented local/IKS practice found specifically for okra damping-off. A strong candidate for direct farmer interviews.

cultural.summary: Rotate away from okra and its relatives to break the wilt fungus's cycle!
cultural.how: Avoid okra/solanaceous crops in the same soil.

cultural.summary: Keep soil moisture steady, since this fungus loves it too wet!
cultural.how: Control soil moisture, avoid excess humidity around roots.

cultural.summary: Say goodbye to wilted plants right away to stop the fungus from spreading!
cultural.how: Destroy affected plants promptly when spotted.

biological.summary: The same helpful fungus seed coat used for damping-off also fights wilt!
biological.how: Treat seed/soil with Trichoderma harzianum before sowing.

botanical.summary: A neem leaf brew tested against wilt fungus, right alongside citrus extract!
botanical.how: Apply neem leaf aqueous extract at sowing and during early growth.
botanical.frequency: At sowing, repeat as needed during early growth

local_practice.note: No documented local/IKS practice found specifically for okra Fusarium wilt. Flagged for farmer interviews.

cultural.summary: Good airflow between plants keeps powdery mildew from settling in!
cultural.how: Ensure good spacing between plants at sowing.

cultural.summary: Feed plants a balanced diet, since too much nitrogen invites mildew!

biological.note: No confirmed microbial bio-agent trial found specifically for okra powdery mildew. Worth testing Pseudomonas fluorescens/Trichoderma here too, since both are confirmed effective against Cercospora leaf spot in okra, but this hasn't been directly tested for powdery mildew yet.

botanical.summary: A neem seed extract spray to keep white powdery spots from spreading!
botanical.how: Spray neem seed kernel extract (NSKE) at 5% concentration.

botanical.summary: A simple lime water spray, a classic okra grower's trick against mildew!
botanical.how: Spray 10% lime water solution on affected leaves.

local_practice.summary: The same traditional cow urine spray, trusted here too for keeping mildew away!
local_practice.how: Spray 10% cow urine solution on the plant.

iks.note: No classical-text-specific formula identified for okra powdery mildew (okra postdates Vrikshayurveda). General tonics like Panchagavya/Nimastra could reasonably be tested here as a hypothesis, but aren't confirmed against this disease specifically in our sources.

iks.summary: A powerful fermented neem-and-cow-gift potion for all-around plant protection!
iks.how: Ferment 5kg crushed neem leaves + 100L water + 5L cow urine + 2kg fresh cow dung, stirring twice daily for 48 hours in shade, then strain. Makes enough for 1 acre.

iks.summary: A spicier fermented potion with chili and tobacco for extra pest-fighting power!
iks.how: Ferment 5kg neem leaves + 20L cow urine + 500g tobacco leaves + 500g green chilies + ginger.
iks.frequency: Same general application pattern as Nimastra

iks.summary: A simple four-ingredient tonic passed down for generations of healthy soil!
iks.how: Ferment cow dung, cow urine, jaggery, and water together.
iks.frequency: Applied as soil drench or diluted foliar spray

iks.summary: A gentle five-ingredient cow tonic no animal harmed, just cow-given gifts!
iks.how: Ferment cow milk, curd, ghee, cow urine, and cow dung together, then dilute before use.
iks.frequency: Soil drench or diluted foliar spray, typically 3-10% concentration
